boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Gonzaga spaces for quiet study, group work, creative projects, campus involvement, and student events, with access governed by each facility.

cards.entity_name: John and Joan Bollier Family Center for Integrated Science and Engineering
cards.title: Take the Window Seat Above Lake Arthur
cards.subtitle: Second-floor study space in the Bollier Center
cards.notes: Head to the second-floor windows for a study session overlooking Lake Arthur; use the outdoor tables when weather and building access permit.
cards.short_summary: A bright indoor study stop paired with seasonal outdoor tables beside the science building.
cards.evidence_claim: A Gonzaga student identified the Bollier Center's second-floor window area and outdoor tables as places to study while overlooking the lake.
cards.access_notes: Use during authorized building access; outdoor tables are weather-dependent.

cards.title: Bring a Group to the Whiteboards
cards.subtitle: Screen-equipped study rooms in the health partnership building
cards.notes: Use a study room with friends when available, and bring notes you can organize across the room's large whiteboard and display screen.
cards.short_summary: Quiet collaboration rooms support visual planning and small-group review sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga's campus study-spots feature says the building has quiet study rooms equipped with screens and large whiteboards for individual or group work.
cards.access_notes: Room availability and building access may depend on university schedules and affiliation.

cards.title: Match the Floor to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Three floors with distinct conversation and quiet-study zones
cards.notes: Work with classmates on the first floor, then move to the quieter third floor when the assignment calls for sustained individual focus.
cards.short_summary: Different noise zones let students switch between collaborative and silent work without leaving the library.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga identifies Foley Library as a student study place with three floors, different noise levels, whiteboards, printers, tables, and academic-support resources.
cards.access_notes: Visitor periods are designated; group rooms are restricted to current Gonzaga students, faculty, and staff.

cards.title: Mirror Your Laptop for Group Review
cards.subtitle: First-floor collaborative workspace in the Rosauer Center
cards.notes: Claim an open table or booth, connect a laptop to a monitor for group review, and keep any drink covered while you work.
cards.short_summary: Flexible seating, shared displays, and charging points make this a practical project-work base.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga says the first-floor Active Learning Center has lounge, table, and booth seating, four monitors for laptop mirroring, and charging stations for study.
cards.source_title: J.M. and Jessie Rosauer Center for Education
cards.access_notes: Use during authorized Rosauer Center access; food is allowed, and drinks must have lids.

cards.title: Use the Student Center as a Flexible Base
cards.subtitle: Lounges, meeting areas, dining, and programming under one roof
cards.notes: Settle into a lounge between classes, meet collaborators in a common area, or check the day's programming before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: The student center combines informal work areas with meeting, dining, and event facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga describes Hemmingson as a meeting place with dining, meeting space, lounges, and programming facilities for studying and gathering.
cards.access_notes: Common-space access is subject to posted hours, university policy, and private-event closures.

cards.title: Move Upstairs for Informal Collaboration
cards.subtitle: Named community spaces above Hemmingson's main level
cards.notes: Take a small group upstairs for conversation or informal project work, and relocate if an event or posted reservation occupies the area.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor community areas offer an alternative to the student center's busier main level.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga's official guide to Hemmingson explicitly invites visitors to use the community spaces on the building's second floor.
cards.source_title: What's Inside the John J. Hemmingson Center
cards.access_notes: Access is subject to Hemmingson hours, posted reservations, and university event policies.

cards.title: Find the Windowed Corner in Hughes Hall
cards.subtitle: Third-floor tables overlooking Bulldog Alley and Herak Lawn
cards.notes: Bring an individual assignment or a small whiteboard problem set, and keep the hallway clear for classes, offices, and laboratory traffic.
cards.short_summary: A window-lined science-building corner combines tables, outlets, a whiteboard, and campus views.
cards.evidence_claim: A Gonzaga student described the Hughes Hall third-floor corner as a study area with tables, chairs, a whiteboard, outlets, and windows over Bulldog Alley and Herak Lawn.
cards.source_title: Gonzaga Students' Favorite Spots on Campus
cards.access_notes: Use only during authorized Hughes Hall access and avoid disrupting nearby laboratories and offices.

cards.title: Prototype a Digital or Hands-On Project
cards.subtitle: Creative technology workspace on Foley Library's lower level
cards.notes: Bring a defined project idea, ask student staff which tool fits it, and confirm current training, scheduling, and material requirements first.
cards.short_summary: The lower-level lab supports digital inquiry, making, experimentation, and project guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga locates the Digital Scholarship Lab on Foley Library's lower level and describes it as an exploratory space for students and faculty using emerging technologies.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current lab availability, equipment training, reservations, and any material charges before starting.

cards.title: Reserve a Room for the Noisy Part
cards.subtitle: Bookable second-floor rooms for collaborative coursework
cards.notes: Reserve the needed time at the circulation desk or by phone, gather at least two students, and keep conversation within the room's noise zone.
cards.short_summary: Eleven reservable rooms give current Gonzaga groups a defined place for discussion and shared work.
cards.evidence_claim: Foley Library's policy documents 11 group study rooms available for one-, two-, or three-hour checkout and additional first-come study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to current Gonzaga students, faculty, and staff; reservations and group-priority rules apply.

cards.title: Check the Campus Calendar for a Globe Room Event
cards.subtitle: Large student-activity and guest-speaker venue in Cataldo Hall
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled student activity or guest speaker, arrive through Cataldo Hall, and treat the room as event-only when it is reserved.
cards.short_summary: A windowed campus venue hosts organized student activities, speakers, dances, and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Gonzaga says the Globe Room is in Cataldo Hall and hosts student activities, dances, guest speakers, and other social events.
cards.access_notes: Enter for scheduled or authorized events; the venue may be unavailable during private reservations or setup.

warnings: Coordinates are null unless directly verifiable from a supporting official source; two building-level coordinates use established campus location data.
Event, room, and building availability can change; users should check posted access information before visiting.
The Globe Room may host varied events, but this card recommends only under-21-safe university activities and guest-speaker programs.
